t2i_prompt: A 1440 px wide desktop website section as a flat straight-on UI mockup in Swiss International Typographic Style on a white page. A large light-weight sans headline in sentence case and a small tagline. Below, a strict grid of square-cornered tiles, one row per item: a deep navy tile with a huge light numeral and steel-blue slash, then limestone tiles of short monospace text with a small label for <CONTENT>, separated by spacer tiles in a checkerboard of navy, limestone and white. Two spacer tiles hold small hairline equipment line drawings. Flat, no shadows.
signature_idea: Situation, need and starting page read across a Swiss checkerboard, each row anchored by a huge slash numeral and two tiles holding blueprint drawings.
strengths: router logic is clear: read across a row to the page to start on
huge light slash numerals, mono text and navy/limestone tiles are on-brand
drawing tiles break the grid with equipment context
maps to a token-only CSS grid
weaknesses: half the tiles are empty spacers, the checkerboard is busy and wastes width
repeated label in every tile is redundant; should be column headers
drawings are tiny and do not relate to their rows
white tiles add a third ground colour
brand_fit_why: Swiss navy/limestone tiles, light numerals, mono text and square corners fit the brand, but the busy empty checkerboard costs calm and space.
